correctness.rationale: For each integer \(r\ge1\), the degree-r symmetric power of the Fibonacci companion matrix is integral and unimodular, so its characteristic polynomial has unit constant; sliding differences at positive indices therefore force their zero-index difference as well. For odd k,r, Cassini yields the contradiction 1=-1 modulo every hypothetical odd prime divisor. Fibonacci periods 3 modulo 2 and 6 modulo 4 supply exact 2-adic gcd. The proof covers every positive odd \(r,k\). The included Python test passed all 372 chosen parameter pairs and is only finite corroboration.

originality.rationale: The checked 2021 paper treats the first power, and the checked 2022 paper treats squares and raises higher powers without giving the uniform odd-power result. Matching outputs at two isolated exponents cannot cover all odd exponents. Searches by direct claim, shift-period alias, exponent parity, and companion-matrix mechanism found no equivalent published-finding corpus statement. Unindexed equivalent work remains a named risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent older or unindexed theorem on powered Fibonacci periodicity might imply the odd-exponent result without matching its window-gcd terminology.
Only the inspected material, not all mathematical literature, can be compared; independent originality assessment has not been performed.

value.rationale: The theorem gives the complete natural odd-exponent/odd-window gcd classification uniformly over two unbounded parameters and supplies an exact finite-prefix reduction, addressing higher-power extensions raised in arXiv:2204.12626. The sharp parity boundary matters: fourth powers with length 25 have a common factor 5. This is a structural explanation and natural classification, not merely a finite table extension. It does not purport to classify even windows or arbitrary Gibonacci initial values.
